housing.summary: Munich is Germany's most expensive rental market. Furnished and unfurnished flats in central districts are scarce and competitive; expect to provide proof of income (Gehaltsnachweise), a SCHUFA credit report and a landlord reference (Mietschuldenfreiheitsbescheinigung). Deposits (Kaution) are legally capped at three months' cold rent.

banking.summary: Opening a German current account (Girokonto) typically requires a registered address, so most newcomers complete the Anmeldung first. Both branch banks and app-based banks operate in Munich; a tax ID and residence permit help with full account features.

schools.summary: Munich offers German public (state) schools plus a strong cluster of international schools serving expatriate families. International options teach English-medium and IB/British/American curricula alongside the Bavarian state system.

legal_admin.summary: New residents must register their address (Anmeldung) at the city's citizen office. Registration is mandatory, usually within two weeks of moving in, and produces the Meldebescheinigung needed for banking, tax and residence-permit steps.
legal_admin.registration_step: Anmeldung (address registration) at the Burgerburo / KVR, typically within 14 days of moving in

tax_finance.summary: After registering, residents are issued a tax identification number automatically by post. Employees are assigned a tax class and file with the local tax office; the Steuer-ID is required for payroll and most financial services.

transport.summary: Munich has an extensive integrated public transport network (U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram and bus) governed by a single fare union. The nationwide Deutschlandticket also covers local transit. Health coverage requires enrolling in statutory or private health insurance and choosing a GP (Hausarzt).
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences remain valid; non-EU licences generally must be exchanged, sometimes requiring a theory and/or practical test depending on the country of origin.
transport.healthcare_registration: Enrol in statutory health insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, e.g. TK, AOK) or private cover, then register with a local GP (Hausarzt).
